identity.title: Mapping the Tibetan Plateau microbiome across ecosystems provides a resource for biodiscovery.

content.abstract: Microbial genetics can inspire innovations in biotechnology, but many microbial communities remain poorly understood. The genetic repertoire of high-mountain microbiomes remains largely untapped for biotechnology. Here we present the Tibetan Environmental Genome (TEG) catalogue, comprising 51,921 metagenome-assembled genomes from 1,698 environmental samples spanning 868 sites across 6 terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems of the Tibetan Plateau, Earth's highest and largest mountain region. The TEG spans 105 phyla encompassing 17,920 species, of which nearly 90% are previously uncharacterized. Importantly, TEG establishes a comprehensive repository for biodiscovery, revealing 44,719 biosynthetic gene clusters, 19,168 candidate antimicrobial peptides, 1,262 low-identity CRISPR-Cas systems and 1,077 candidate polyethylene terephthalate hydrolases. To validate these findings, 29 candidate antimicrobial peptides were synthesized and all exhibited inhibitory activity against at least 1 of 7 tested pathogens, with 5 showing broad-spectrum activity. This catalogue reveals a rich and previously inaccessible pool of enzymes, bioactive compounds and programmable molecular systems, establishing a foundational resource for discovery and application in biotechnology.
